modalLead: The keyboard reads as one set of rules now: every action on a bookmark is Shift plus a letter, bare letters act on the first press, and the right-click menu shows the key beside each entry so the keys can be picked up without looking them up.

items.text: Every row action is Shift plus a letter. Inline edit is Shift+E and the preview card is Shift+V — they were ; and [, two keys that said nothing about what they do. Sharing moves to Shift+L, so Shift+S opens config wherever you press it instead of meaning one thing with a bookmark selected and another without. The old keys still work; they are simply no longer the ones taught.

The right-click menu shows the key. Every entry that has one now carries it beside the label — open in a new tab, copy, share, edit, pin, tags, move, checking, Show in Health, delete. The category menu has done this for a while; the bookmark menu had eleven keys and showed none of them.

A letter acts as soon as you press it. c adds a category and g starts the jump to one; both used to wait out a short hold so a quick tap could reach the shortcut search instead. What that costs: a bookmark whose shortcut starts with c, g, j, k, t or x is reached by opening search first with >.
k and j move the highlight, next to the arrow keys — the same pair that has always worked in the config lists and in Health.

Reach a category header without the mouse. Shift+Home steps up from the list to the header above it, where F2 renames, Shift+W spreads it across columns, Delete deletes it and Shift+F10 opens its menu. Delete on a header used to open the menu, which is the one place a Delete key meant "show me the options".

The menu opens next to the row. Raised from the keyboard — the Menu key, or Shift+F10 — both the bookmark and the category menu appeared in the top-left corner of the window, nowhere near what they were about.
Shift+W with nothing selected does nothing. It used to spread whichever category happened to be first on the page.
The printable sheet is readable again. It was printing the long explanations from the cheat sheet window instead of the short ones written for paper, so rows ran past the width they were meant for.
Three keys join the printed sheet: k and j beside the arrows, Shift+E for inline edit, and Shift+Home for the category header.

Read the activity log in the app. Data & backups → Server log has a new choice under Show: Activity only. Those lines — a bookmark saved, a page added, a check run — were already in there, mixed in with the request traffic, findable only if you knew to search for the word. Needs Collect server log switched on, because it is the same log.
Help → About has somewhere to go. The nextDash wordmark, and three addresses: the project at nextdash.cc, issues and release notes on GitHub, and the person who writes it at jordibrw.nl.

The optional usage snapshot says more, and still says nothing about you. With analytics switched on it now reports which settings you run and roughly how large your library is. Every number is rounded into a band — a library of 1274 bookmarks reports as 500+ — and a custom theme reports as custom rather than by its own identifier, which was distinctive enough to follow one install between releases. Switched off, nothing is counted at all: the count is not gathered and then discarded, it is never taken. Behavior → Privacy is where the switch lives.
Category headers stopped being taller than they need to be. A header carrying the + button was a hair taller than one without it.
The recent-bookmarks key keeps out of the way. * now leaves the key alone while something else is open, the way the cheat sheet and collapse-all keys already did.
